alert_background_failed_task_checks.milestone: EP-ALERT bounded Android scheduled failed-task parity
alert_background_failed_task_checks.behavior: For a certificate-verified saved connection with scheduled checks enabled, the operator may separately opt into bounded recent-task scanning. Each eligible WorkManager run reuses the authenticated node list, checks at most 16 nodes and requests at most 20 recent task rows per node. The option defaults off for legacy policies. New definite failures are detected relative to the last complete task end-time watermark, so a later failure can notify while an older failure remains visible.
alert_background_failed_task_checks.contract: GET /api2/json/cluster/resources?type=node plus optional GET /api2/json/nodes/{node}/tasks?limit=20&source=all only; redirects disabled; no mutation methods; 10-second connect/read timeouts; 512 KiB cap per successful response; no immediate WorkManager retry.
alert_background_failed_task_checks.semantics: RUNNING is non-incident; terminal OK is healthy; explicit terminal non-OK results are incidents. Bare stopped without exit status and unknown status remain unknown rather than becoming failed-task incidents, matching the foreground RecentServerTask parser. A definite failure also requires a positive endtime for occurrence ordering. Complete scans advance a per-profile latest-terminal-endtime watermark; a failure is newly observed only when newer than the previous complete watermark. Incomplete task reads never advance that watermark or clear prior task incident state. Independently complete node-state transitions remain effective when task reads are incomplete.
alert_background_failed_task_checks.privacy: Native occurrence state stores profile-scoped node/task category booleans plus one latest complete task end-time integer watermark. No UPID, task type, resource ID, node/guest name, VMID, log, credential or raw PVE response is persisted or inserted into notifications/navigation.

alert_scheduled_node_cpu_thresholds.milestone: EP-ALERT bounded Android scheduled node-CPU threshold parity
alert_scheduled_node_cpu_thresholds.behavior: For a certificate-verified saved connection with scheduled checks enabled, the operator may separately opt into evaluation of enabled node-CPU threshold rules. The worker reuses the existing authenticated cluster node snapshot and adds no PVE endpoint. Up to 32 node-CPU rules are evaluated with their saved 1-10 consecutive-sample confirmation and 0-20 percentage-point hysteresis controls. Guest CPU and storage-usage rules remain foreground-only.
alert_scheduled_node_cpu_thresholds.state_machine: Inactive rules increment pending confirmation only on usable CPU samples at or above the firing threshold; usable samples below threshold reset pending confirmation. Active rules resolve below threshold when hysteresis is zero or at/below threshold-minus-hysteresis when positive. Missing/unusable samples reset pending confirmation but do not resolve an active rule. A missing opted-in rule sample makes the threshold side incomplete and prevents last-complete-check advancement.
alert_scheduled_node_cpu_thresholds.synchronization: Saving, enabling, disabling or deleting a foreground threshold rule synchronizes the native worker copy without counting as a sample. If native synchronization fails while a schedule is active, AppController disables scheduled monitoring rather than allowing stale background rule configuration to continue silently. When no schedule is active, synchronization is a no-op.
alert_scheduled_node_cpu_thresholds.privacy: Only enabled node-CPU rule ID, node selector, threshold percent, consecutive-sample count and hysteresis percent are copied, and only inside the existing AES-256-GCM Android-Keystore-encrypted worker payload. Runtime threshold state is stored in private native preferences under SHA-256 hashes of rule IDs and contains bounded pending counters plus active booleans only. Display labels, guest/storage identifiers, sampled CPU values, credentials and incident details are not stored in runtime threshold state or notification/navigation payloads.
alert_scheduled_node_cpu_thresholds.contract: Reuses GET /api2/json/cluster/resources?type=node only; redirects disabled; no POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE; existing 10-second connect/read timeouts, 512 KiB response cap, network constraint and no immediate WorkManager retry remain unchanged. Notifications remain generic and use the existing quiet-hours, lock-screen privacy, generic Incidents navigation and shared cross-mode delivery cooldown.

alert_scheduled_guest_cpu_thresholds.milestone: EP-ALERT bounded Android scheduled guest-CPU threshold parity
alert_scheduled_guest_cpu_thresholds.behavior: For a certificate-verified saved connection with scheduled checks enabled, the operator may separately opt into enabled guest-CPU threshold rules. When at least one enabled guest rule exists the worker performs one bounded GET /cluster/resources?type=vm, matches exact qemu/lxc + node + VMID identities, and applies the saved consecutive-sample and hysteresis controls. Storage-usage rules remain foreground-only.
alert_scheduled_guest_cpu_thresholds.state_machine: Missing, malformed or duplicate guest samples make the guest threshold component incomplete; pending confirmation resets while an already-active incident is preserved. Active rules clear only at the same hysteresis boundary used by the existing threshold engine.
alert_scheduled_guest_cpu_thresholds.synchronization: Flutter sends node and guest scheduled rule sets through one atomic syncThresholdRules channel. Native validation enforces unique rule IDs across categories and at most 32 combined rules; synchronization failure disables scheduled monitoring fail-closed.
